brief: Deutsche Bank's weekly positioning tracker: aggregate equity positioning held at modestly overweight (60th percentile) despite the surge in rates volatility, but the composite masks a split. Large-cap positioning stayed overweight (85th percentile, still below levels the earnings boom would imply) while small caps slipped to modestly underweight (43rd percentile). Systematic strategies held near their top decile (92nd percentile) as equity vol stayed subdued, while discretionary positioning fell back below neutral (27th percentile, 68th in large caps alone), a pattern DB says recurs when rates vol rises; DB argues rates vol, not the level of rates, is what matters for equities (correlation to the MOVE index: -62% since 2021). Sector positioning stayed narrow, with MCG & Tech the only overweight; the rotation into Tech added another 2pp this week and is nearing levels from which it has reversed several times before, though not yet at the top of its long-run trend channel. Vol-control funds sit at the 98th percentile with limited room to add and an increasingly asymmetric flow backdrop if volatility rises. Equity fund flows turned positive ($15.8bn) on DM strength even as US funds extended outflows; bond funds drew $18.8bn while money-market funds saw $118bn of outflows.
